title: High-Availability Gaming Backend Distribution
business: Online gaming companies requiring consistent, low-latency connectivity for thousands of concurrent players connecting to stateful game servers.
problem: Individual game server instances are prone to unexpected termination, leading to player disconnection and loss of session state during peak traffic.
solution: Azure Load Balancer provides Layer 4 load balancing to distribute incoming UDP/TCP traffic across a pool of backend virtual machines, ensuring traffic is only routed to healthy instances.
steps: Create a backend pool containing the IP addresses of the game server virtual machines.
Define health probes that periodically check the status of each game server instance.
Configure load balancing rules to map frontend IP ports to the backend pool ports.
Associate the load balancer with a public IP or internal virtual network endpoint.
outcome: Improved service availability where player traffic is automatically rerouted away from unresponsive server instances without manual intervention.
limitation: Azure Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and does not inspect application-layer (HTTP/HTTPS) content; to verify if the application is truly processing requests correctly, you must rely on port-based health probes rather than deep content inspection.

questions.question: In High-Availability Gaming Backend Distribution, how does the technology address the problem of server failure?
options: By rerouting traffic away from unresponsive instances using health probes.
By inspecting the game state at the application layer to fix errors.
By automatically restarting the physical hardware of the server.
By increasing the bandwidth of the individual server instances.
questions.explanation: The solution relies on Layer 4 load balancing to distribute traffic only to healthy instances, which is achieved through health probes.

It is limited to internal network traffic only.
It cannot perform deep application-layer content inspection.
It requires manual intervention to update the backend pool.
